problem:
Arranged in **ascending order**, the solutions of the equation $4\operatorname{cos}⁡x+2=0$ for $0\le x<2\pi ,$ are $x=${{field-1}} and $x=$
{{field-2}}.
worked_solution:
First, we isolate $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4\operatorname{cos}⁡x+2 & =0 \\ 4\operatorname{cos}⁡x & =-2 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡x & =-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arccos}⁡(-\frac{1}{2})=\frac{2\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\frac{2\pi }{3}$ lies inside the required domain, our first solution is $x=\frac{2\pi }{3}.$

Our first solution lies in the second quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{3}.$ Since $\operatorname{cos}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the third quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{3}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13952163/assets/d188a8634c7d33813260472c8691dccdbedbc809d3b59445afc912a43a09675b.png)

Since the second solution $x$ lies in the $3$rd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\pi +{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi +\frac{\pi }{3} \\  & =\frac{4\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solutions of the equation, arranged in ascending order, are $x=\frac{2\pi }{3}$ and $x=\frac{4\pi }{3}.$
